title: The eclipse and the rain
hookLine: special prayers for an eclipse and for rain

cards: The sun went dark over Medina on the day Ibrahim died. He was the son of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. A report in Sahih al-Bukhari says people began to say it: the sun has eclipsed because Ibrahim died.
It would have been easy to let them. It was a kind thing to say, and it honored a grieving father. Instead, on the day of his own loss, the Prophet stood up and corrected them.

teach.b: Islam keeps special prayers for two changes in the sky: the eclipse and the drought. First, what he said. The sun and the moon are two of the signs of God.
They do not eclipse for anyone's death or for anyone's life.
When you see it, pray, and call on God, until it clears. He turned a rumor that flattered him into a prayer pointed away from himself. Second, the eclipse prayer, salat al-kusuf.
Aisha's report in Bukhari describes it prayed in congregation, with very long standing and recitation, and an extra bowing in each unit.
Here the schools differ: the Hanafi school prays it in the form of ordinary units; the other schools follow the reports with the extra bowing. Both pray until the light returns. Third, the rain.
Salat al-istisqa is the prayer asking for rain.

Another report in Bukhari says the Prophet went out to the open prayer ground, faced the qibla, turned his cloak around, and prayed two units. Some scholars read the turned cloak as a hope that the season would turn too.

Fourth, a Friday story, picking up from the khutbah four days ago. During the sermon, a man stood and said the animals were dying and the roads were cut: ask God for rain. The Prophet raised his hands and asked.
The report says rain fell, and kept falling until the next Friday, when a man stood and asked for it to stop.
So the Prophet asked again, for rain around them and not upon them.
Too dark, too dry, too wet: each one met with a prayer.

how: When there is a solar or lunar eclipse, Muslims gather at mosques for the eclipse prayer, with long recitation, until it passes; in times of drought, communities go out to an open prayer ground for the rain prayer.

games.q: what does “the eclipse and the rain” mean?
o: a festival prayer held when the rainy season begins
special prayers for when the sun darkens or rain is needed
a sign in the sky that someone important has just died

games.q: the eclipse and the rain — tap the pairs.

s: the Prophet said the eclipse came because his son died
he said the sun and moon do not eclipse for anyone's death or life.
in the rain prayer, the Prophet turned his cloak around
a report in Sahih al-Bukhari describes it, along with two units and facing the qibla.
the Prophet once asked for the rain to stop falling on the town
after a week of rain, he asked for it around them and not upon them.

games.q: it's the day the Prophet's son Ibrahim has died. the sun goes dark, and people say it's grieving for him. you're the Prophet. what do you say?
o: yes: even the sky mourns my son.
the sun and moon don't eclipse for anyone's death or life. pray.
say nothing, and let them believe it.
games.why: he corrected them on the day of his own grief, and told them to pray and call on God until it cleared (Sahih al-Bukhari).

practice: Look out a window, or remember the last sky you saw, and stay with its color, its light, the clouds or the lack of them, for a few breaths.

If you pray, you might ask a teacher of your school how the eclipse and rain prayers are prayed, and when your mosque holds them. If you don't, let the next change in the weather stop you for one full breath.

wordCard.voice: The eclipse and the rain. Two special prayers, salat al-kusuf when the sun or moon darkens, salat al-istisqa when rain is needed. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: eclipse, especially of the sun. salat al-kusuf is the eclipse prayer.

carryVoice: Your line: every sky has its prayer. The sun and moon are signs, not news about us. Rest well.
